title: I gave Astra-6 control of Blender to help make my stealth RTS game Barbarians. Stop letting civilizations raid your goody huts!
author: SpartanDetermination
selftext:
So I initially started with a general idea of "Civilization, but from the barbarian's perspective."  After a lot of back-and-forth revising and debate, I determined that the concept doesn't work so well as a 4X turn-based game as it would as an RTS. So I took the ball with that and started to experiment with how a game would work where your opponent get's more technologically advanced as time goes by, increases in number & strength, and keeps expanding. 

  
The solution was to make this a "tactics"-based RTS. You employ stealth (if you can) to carry out missions (ie, steal horses from the Roman centurians, burn down Greek boats, steal grain from English cities). So you lead a small band on raids, watch patrols, sneak through cover, knock out guards, recover supplies, and get your kidnapped people home. Once you steal horses, you can start having mounted units. Steal steel armor and you can start to experiment with it. Plus you can pause the game & issue orders that take effect right after you unpause. You can set off an alarm, and ambush the enemy troops that go to investigate, or try to spend the entire time in stealth to accomplish your goals. 

  
So I worked with codex using Astra 6 to code the backend and bug-test. Afterwards I let Astra run Blender to make the art assets, as well as set up the look of the 4 seasons and their general ambience. Rain can mask footsteps, while snow lets your enemies track you. It took a lot of handholding to get the blender system running right. It seems like the frontier LLM's can handle/interpret lighting effects and shade perfectly, but struggle with aesthetic interpretation of the art assets. So we must have gone through 30 revisions of the tree assets before finally reaching a decent outcome. 

  
Five campaigns, with 31 chapters, facing powers inspired by Rome, China, Spain, Greece, and England. It’s a warm, mischievous take on the subject, not a grim historical war simulator. I released it on iphone/ipad as well as Steam so that kids can play it.
